Omission of a merely definitional transcription is justified by the record's stated reason, without treating its audit-history note as part of the claim.

These are exactly admissible objects under the standing assumptions, which impose neither finite support nor integrability. This contradicts the canonical universal ordinary-mean existence assertion itself. The theorem is a correct refutation of that assertion, not an assertion that totalized mean identities fail.
